The implementation is complete and fully validated. Here's a summary of what I built:

## Architecture

**Python driver** (`main.py`, `protocol.py`, `solver.py`, `native.py`):
- Strict request validation (duplicate keys, NaN/Infinity, extra JSON values, type/range/domain bounds) rejecting the whole request with exactly `{"error":"invalid"}`.
- Immutable FIB history: route aliasing/normalization, last-row-wins, ordered transactions (each commits a version, even empty ones), covering routes preserved so withdrawals reveal the right fallback.
- Canonical atlas compilation with exact 128-bit arithmetic (boundary sweep + longest-prefix max-heap).
- Domain checks that require compilation: `R ≤ 64` per version, `≤ 128` summed over all versions of all cases.
- Forwarding changes (sorted, disjoint, coalesced, `U` bounds), burst answer paths and the exact objective.

**C++17 scalar library** (`engine.hpp`, `engine.cpp`):
- `ATLAS` — full-width maximal forwarding runs (`unsigned __int128`).
- `PACK`/`TRACE` — exact FIDX image construction and byte-level packed lookup.
- `SOLVE` — the joint optimiser.

## The optimiser
An exact interval DP over `[i,j)` run ranges: node options (leaf span 1..8 / internal fanout 2..9, encoding modes 0–2 with the 2⁶⁴/2³² spread legality tests, cached/uncached) are combined with children forests, carrying a resident-page dimension as a monotone array merged by min-plus convolution. The lexicographic `(work, image_pages)` pair is carried in one integer as `work·PAGE_WEIGHT + pages`, so both objectives are minimized jointly and exactly. Versions are coupled only through the shared page budget, folded with the same convolution, then the allocation is back-tracked and each tree is reconstructed by exact value matching, re-ordered breadth-first and packed.

The burst-aware cost model computes the fetch weight `T` from each burst's own next-run cursor — necessary because a burst whose runs straddle a node range without entering it must fetch nothing.

## Validation
- All public JSON and native fixtures pass the supplied auditor (`check.py`'s own decode/audit path, since `kill` is denied in this shell).
- ~600 random requests verified against an **independent exhaustive planner** (all trees/modes/cached subsets) — exact optimality confirmed.
- ~350 requests audited against ~40 random legal layouts each at `R = 64` (clustered and spread).
- Native `PACK`/`TRACE` byte-identical to an independent Python builder; `ATLAS` cross-checked.
- 61 malformed/edge inputs, worst-case batches (128 runs, 256 bursts, 8192 addresses, 59990 rows) all under 3 s of the 120 s budget.
